chunks: Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said to a man: “What do these people say about a man when he misses the two rak‘ahs with the Imam?”
I said: “They say he recites in the two rak‘ahs al-Hamd and a surah.” So he said: “This turns his salat around, making its beginning its end.”
I said: “So how should he act?” He said: “He recites Fatihat al-Kitab in every rak‘ah.”

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَانِ: the two units of prayer that were missed
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.بِالْحَمْدِ: Surah al-Fatihah, referred to here by al-Hamd
key_terms.سُورَةٍ: an additional surah recited after al-Fatihah
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat, whose correct order must be preserved
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: the Opening of the Book, that is Surah al-Fatihah
key_terms.فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ: in every rak‘ah, indicating the prescribed recitation here

ai.seo_question: How should a person recite in congregational salat if he missed two rak‘ahs with the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about how a latecomer in congregational salat should recite after missing two rak‘ahs with the Imam. Imam Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Baqir عليه السلام rejects a method that would invert the order of the prayer and instructs that Fatihat al-Kitab be recited in each rak‘ah.
